Senses.Explanation: A formulaic “take care.” In recorded sayings named teachers end hall addresses, informal convocations, addresses to the assembly, or whisk talks with it and step down. Recurrent formulas include “You have stood long, kind assembly; I humbly hope you take care; he stepped down,” and the shorter “Take care; he then stepped down.” It is also a parting word in dialogue: an unnamed departing participant says “take care” and leaves. A written final statement closes, “I humbly hope you take care” (伏惟珍重), before its author puts down the brush and asks whether to depart sitting or lying. This leave-taking formula is a separate speech act from the transitive verb “to treasure” an object.
Senses.Note: Primary corpus deployment: a formulaic close and parting word, not a specialized technical term. The curated passages show a whisk talk, a hall address, an address to the assembly, and an unnamed participant's farewell. The headword has 3,863 hits in 351 allowlisted texts; this high-frequency formula is distinct from the rarer transitive verb.

Occurrences.Kwic: 久立眾慈，伏惟珍重。下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of Guiding Principles from the Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), Folang Xing's end-of-retreat whisk address. Folang is the exact speaker who closes his own appraisal of Dongshan's verse by looking over the assembly, shouting, warning against speaking dreams before fools, and saying farewell.
The Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), in Zhaozhou Congshen's record. Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact speaker closing his hall address with the formula 'take care.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 與大眾舉一古人方便。珍重便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Luohan Guichen as the actor for this occurrence.

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fenyang Wude (汾陽無德禪師語錄). The exact actor is an unnamed departing monk who says farewell and leaves, after which Fenyang supplies a substitute reply. No personal name remains after the six-rung review.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今吾如是，豈不快哉！塵勞外緣，一時掃盡。荷諸山垂顧，咸願證明。伏惟珍重。置筆顧簡堂曰：某坐去好，臥去好？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), layman Qian Duanli biography. Qian Duanli is the exact author of the written final declaration that asks whether any buddha, patriarch, old teacher, or good knowing adviser can leap over this move and closes by bidding the assembled teachers farewell.

Senses.Explanation: A transitive verb meaning to treasure or value an object. Letters and prefaces record “treasure the teaching gate” (珍重法門), “treasure this record and circulate it widely” (珍重此錄，廣為流佈), and “if [you] wish to value that matter” (若欲珍重其事). Unlike the stock closing “take care,” these clauses name what is valued.
Senses.Note: The three independently sourced objects establish the distinct action of valuing something, not merely a grammatical variant or interpretation of the leave-taking formula. No special Chan deviation beyond the corpus objects is asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 屢承翰教，珍重法門，筆舌難盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄), Poshan Haiming's reply-letter to academy chancellor Tan Sao'an. Poshan Haiming is the exact author, thanking his correspondent for repeated written instruction and for treating the teaching gate with care.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又能珍重此錄，廣為流佈
Occurrences.AttributionNote: an unnamed Chan practitioner from Jiahe is the exact actor. Drafts from Chan Master Weilin Daopei's Traveling Hermitage (為霖禪師旅泊菴稿), Weilin Daopei's preface to Daqian's recorded sayings. The exact grammatical actor is the Chan practitioner identified only as being from Jiahe: Weilin says that this practitioner had long trained under the hammer and whisk, cherished the record, and spread it widely. All six rungs supply no personal name for him.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: an unnamed Chan practitioner from Jiahe
ActorAttribution.ActorRole: preserver and publisher of Daqian's record

Occurrences.Kwic: 若欲珍重其事，且放過諸人一著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Sheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄), New Year's Eve informal address. Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker of the stored counsel that, if his listeners wish to treat the matter with due care, he will first let them off one move.
